title: Two Players Take Piles From the Ends: Who Wins by How Much?

concept.title: The value of a position is the difference between the player to move and the other player
body: Piles of stones stand in a row. Two players move in turns; in each turn the player takes **one whole pile from the left end or from the right end** and adds the stones to their own score. The game ends when no pile is left. Both players play perfectly to maximise **their own score minus the score of the other player**. Print the best possible difference for the player who moves first. For the piles `5 3 4 5` the first player gets 9 and the second gets 8: the difference is 1.

Define the state by the remaining piles `i .. j`. Let `diff(i, j)` be the largest value of (score of the player to move) - (score of the other player) that the player to move can force from this state. If the player takes the left pile `a[i]`, the other player moves next in `i + 1 .. j` and gets the advantage `diff(i + 1, j)`, so the advantage of the first one is `a[i] - diff(i + 1, j)`. Taking the right pile gives `a[j] - diff(i, j - 1)`: **`diff(i, j) = max(a[i] - diff(i + 1, j), a[j] - diff(i, j - 1))`**, and `diff(i, i) = a[i]`. This "the opponent plays the same game" recurrence is the whole minimax idea in one line.

body.code:
diff = a[:]                                        # length 1: diff(i, i) = a[i]
for length in range(2, n + 1):
    diff = [max(a[i] - diff[i + 1], a[i + length - 1] - diff[i]) for i in range(n - length + 1)]
print(diff[0])

body: Here `diff[i]` after processing the length `L` stands for `diff(i, i + L - 1)`; the new `diff[i]` needs the old `diff[i + 1]` (the range `i + 1 .. i + L - 1`) and the old `diff[i]` (the range `i .. i + L - 2`), so a single array that shrinks by one each round is enough: O(n^2) time, O(n) memory. If the answer is positive, the first player wins; if it is zero, the game is a draw in points.

statement: `n` piles of stones stand in a row. Two players alternately take one pile from the left end or from the right end of the row and add its stones to their own score, until no pile is left. Both play optimally to maximise their own score minus the other's score. Print the largest value of (first player's score - second player's score) that the first player can guarantee.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the number of piles.
The second line has `n` numbers: the number of stones in each pile.
outputFormat: Print the best score difference for the first player.

examples.note: The first player takes 5; whatever the second player does, the first ends with 9 against 8: the difference is 1.

hints: Let diff(i, j) be the best (mover - opponent) score difference on the piles i to j.
Taking the left pile gives a[i] - diff(i + 1, j); taking the right pile gives a[j] - diff(i, j - 1).
One array that gets shorter by one each round is enough.

explanation: diff(i, j), the largest (score of the player to move) - (score of the other player) on the piles i..j, is max(a[i] - diff(i + 1, j), a[j] - diff(i, j - 1)) with diff(i, i) = a[i]; a single array shrinking by one per round holds the values of the current length, and diff(0, n - 1) is the answer.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

diff = a[:]
for length in range(2, n + 1):
    diff = [max(a[i] - diff[i + 1], a[i + length - 1] - diff[i]) for i in range(n - length + 1)]
print(diff[0])
